What it does: How much darker some copies are than others, from 0 (all the same) to 1. 0.1 darkens each copy by up to 10 percent. Used while painting.

A color the copies are tinted, as three small fields: red, green and blue, each from 0 to 1. 1, 1, 1 is white, which means no tint. 0.8, 1, 0.6 makes grass a fresher green, and 1, 0.9, 0.6 makes it dry and yellow.

How far each copy's color may turn around the color wheel, in degrees either way, chosen at random for each copy. At 20, some tufts are greener and some yellower. It turns the tint, so it shows only when the tint isn't white.

How much copies sway: how far a point moves sideways for each unit of height above the copy's base. The base stays still and the tip moves most, and copies near each other don't sway together. Try 0.05 to 0.1 for grass and 0.02 to 0.05 for trees. 0 keeps them still.
Which way the wind blows, in degrees around the up direction: 0 along the x axis, 90 along the z axis.
